newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda expected to export 14,300 tonnes of cotton.
newsitem.headline: Uganda expected to export 14,300 tonnes of cotton.

text.p: Uganda's Cotton Development Organisation (CDO) said on Tuesday the country would produce 18,500 tonnes of cotton in 1996/97 of which 14,430 would be exported in 1996
It was correcting figures released earlier which gave bales as tonnes and thus exaggerated 1996/97 production and exports.
The 14,430 tonnes of cotton lint compared with 9,385 exported out of the 1995/96 production total of 10,436 tonnes, the CDO said.

The World Bank injected $31 million for cotton development in Uganda over a five-year period from 1994 after liberalisation through the International Development Agency, the International Fund for Agricultural Development and the Ugandan government.
Uganda reached peak cotton production in 1969/70 with a total of 86,353 tonnes of lint of which 80,639 were exported.
In 1987/88 cotton production dropped to 2,160 tonnes of which 887 were exported.
